bib.title: When to Retrieve: Teaching LLMs to Utilize Information Retrieval Effectively

question: Can an LLM learn to decide by itself when a question needs an external retriever and when its parametric memory suffices?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning an LLM on data labelled by where its zero-shot answers fail teaches it to emit a special RET token exactly when it needs extra context.
contributions: Comparable to popularity-threshold strategy without using popularity scores
Model retrieves effectively when it asks and answers accurately when it does not
IR system quality is the main bottleneck (gold vs retrieved passages)

method.summary: Llama-2 7B is zero-shot tested on a QA training set; questions it gets wrong become two training instances (parametric prompt with target <RET>, and context prompt with gold passage and answer), correct ones keep the gold answer. The model is LoRA-fine-tuned on this and at inference emits <RET> to trigger Contriever top-1 retrieval and a second prompt.

limits: Evaluated only on PopQA with one 7B model; no larger models or other test sets.
Retrieves a single top-1 Contriever passage; authors concede retrieval quality is the bottleneck and multiple passages would help.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; gains over always-retrieve are 0.9 to 1.6 points.
ADAPT-LLM(NQ) at 35.30% is below the popularity method (36.81%); 'comparable' claim only.
Retrieval decision is learned from a single zero-shot pass of the base model; calibration of RET not studied. RET issued for 82-87% of questions so IR savings are modest.
Why SQuAD transfers better than NQ is not explained (guessed to be scale).
Cost and latency of retrieval not measured.

terms.definition: LLM fine-tuned to emit <RET> when it needs context and otherwise answer directly

code.snippet: for q, gold_ans, pass in (Q, A, P): ans = LLM(q); if ans = gold_ans: add(parametric_prompt, q, gold_ans) else: add(parametric_prompt, q, "<RET>"); add(context_prompt, q, gold_ans, pass)
